title: Architecture Drift Detection Model — First Formal Specification
authority: PROJECT_CONSTITUTION.md; S208 Board A Frozen Principles
sources_consumed: SESSION208_ARCHITECTURAL_PRINCIPLES.json — 6 frozen principles with violation detection criteria
knowledge/DEFECT_LIBRARY.md — DL-008, DL-019, DL-029, DL-035, DL-036 as drift case studies
knowledge/CURRENT_BASELINES.md — 15 runtime file hashes as drift detection baseline
purpose: This model defines the 6 categories of architecture drift, their detection signals, automated checks, severity, and response protocols. It is the first formal drift model for the CMA Part 1 Exam Simulator. Its purpose is to detect when Framework v2 principles are being eroded — not to prevent all defects, but to prevent architecture-level regression.

drift_categories.description: Two or more files claim authority for the same entity type with divergent data
drift_categories.principle_violated: P6 Traceability Everywhere + P2 Scan Once Consume Many

historical_evidence.note: No confirmed duplicate registry incidents. This is a preventive category defined by the P2 principle (single source of truth).
historical_evidence.near_miss: DL-033: naming confusion between 'Pack E' (file) and 'Pack A Section E' (section) caused Wave 4 to check wrong file. This was a naming/labeling issue, not a duplicate registry — but demonstrates the risk.

detection_signals.signal: Two files in the project contain entity lists for the same entity type with different item counts
detection_signals.automated_check: Cross-reference entity-type identifiers across all JSON/MD files in knowledge/, reports/, and scripts/output/ directories. Flag any pair of files with overlapping entity types but divergent counts.
detection_signals.frequency: Per session or per certification wave

detection_signals.signal: A new tool or script generates its own entity list rather than consuming MASTER_QUESTION_REGISTRY.md
detection_signals.automated_check: Audit new scripts for QID extraction logic. If they parse raw pack files independently rather than consuming generated artifacts, flag immediately.

response_protocol.immediate: Halt all operations that consume from the duplicate registry. Cross-reference both sources against raw pack files. Designate the authoritative source per SESSION208_REGISTRY_AUTHORITY.json.
response_protocol.remediation: Retire the non-authoritative registry. Update all consumers to reference the authoritative source. Document the incident.
response_protocol.prevention: All new registries must be registered in SESSION208_REGISTRY_AUTHORITY.json before use. Registry authority model is the gatekeeper.

drift_categories.description: The same structural scan is executed multiple times by different agents or tools within the same session, producing divergent results
drift_categories.principle_violated: P2 Scan Once Consume Many + P3 Delta Review

DL-008_scan_redundancy.root_cause: No scan artifact reuse. Each agent independently re-scanned raw pack files with its own parsing methodology.
DL-008_scan_redundancy.impact: Divergent DL-008 counts (10 vs 342 vs 539 vs 0) across sessions — each using different scan methodology. The 22nd scan was finally the correct one.

DL-026_scan_redundancy.root_cause: 5-agent scoping session (632), Agent 6 boundary-aware re-verification (1,005), enforced-depth autonomous runs (1,056→27→6). Each scan used different methodology.
DL-026_scan_redundancy.impact: Remediation was delayed while the true scope was debated. The 1,005 count (Agent 6, boundary-aware object-level parse) was authoritative.

DL-008_phantom_entries.events: CURRENT_BASELINES.md §3 initially listed 67 CRITICAL DL-008 in learner pool — all were DL-029 forward-scan artifacts (CC-before-QID architecture produced ~75% false-positive rate).
DL-008_phantom_entries.methodology_fix: Function constructor parse confirmed 0 across all 2,500 items. 8 permanent prevention rules established (S802 Agent C).

detection_signals.signal: Two agents in the same session report different defect counts for the same defect class on the same pack
detection_signals.automated_check: Compare defect counts across agent reports within a session. Any divergence > 0 for the same (defect_class, pack) pair is a scan redundancy flag.

detection_signals.signal: A session spawns an agent to re-scan for a defect class that was already scanned earlier in the same session
detection_signals.automated_check: Track scan events per (defect_class, session) — flag any duplicate.

detection_signals.signal: Count instability — the same defect count changes between consecutive scans without content changes
detection_signals.automated_check: Run the scan twice independently. If counts diverge by > 5%, the methodology is unreliable. Require count stability before any remediation action (AGENTS.md §6).

response_protocol.immediate: Halt remediation. Do not execute writes based on unstable counts. Run count a third time. Cross-check methodology between runs (AGENTS.md §6).
response_protocol.remediation: Designate one scan as authoritative using the most rigorous methodology (boundary-aware object-level parse or Function constructor). Produce a scan artifact. All downstream agents consume artifact, not raw files.
response_protocol.prevention: Scan Once principle: the first scan in a session produces the artifact. No re-scanning. Artifact reuse eliminates this entire drift category.

drift_categories.description: Two or more tools produce different readiness/certification/blocks lists for the same content, using different parsing rules
drift_categories.principle_violated: P2 Scan Once Consume Many + P1 Identity Before Trust

DL-036_pipeline_divergence.root_cause: Candidate Engine's Pack E QID regex (/^P1E-[A-F]-\d{3}$/) did not match R-series items (P1-E-R##). Readiness Scorer's regex correctly matched them.
DL-036_pipeline_divergence.impact: 40 Certified items misclassified as BLOCKED by one tool. No learner impact but pipeline unreliability.
DL-036_pipeline_divergence.resolution: S813 C2 — pipeline artifact reuse required. Candidate Engine must consume Readiness Scorer artifact, not independently re-scan.

P1-EC-004_state_inconsistency.root_cause: Registry staleness — Investigation API read from stale registry that predated S853 certification.
P1-EC-004_state_inconsistency.impact: Investigation workbench flagged an anomaly. No learner impact but traceability gap.

detection_signals.signal: Two tools report different BLOCKED/CERTIFY/READY counts for the same pack
detection_signals.automated_check: At each pipeline gate checkpoint, extract per-pack counts from all tools. If counts diverge, flag for reconciliation.

detection_signals.signal: A consumer tool uses a different QID regex or parsing method than the producer tool
detection_signals.automated_check: Audit tool QID regex against MASTER_QUESTION_REGISTRY.md QID format. Any mismatch is a shadow queue risk.
detection_signals.frequency: Per new tool introduction or QID format change

response_protocol.immediate: Isolate the divergent tool. Identify QID list difference (which QIDs are in one queue but not the other). Cross-reference against raw file ground truth.
response_protocol.remediation: Align the consumer tool to the producer tool's output. If the consumer tool must re-scan, use identical parsing methodology. Better: consume the producer's artifact.
response_protocol.prevention: Artifact consumption pipeline — consumer tools never independently re-scan. Single source of truth for QID classification.

drift_categories.description: Items certified into the learner pool without passing automated pre-flight gates — human override of automated governance
drift_categories.principle_violated: P4 Readiness Before Certification + P5 Governance Automation

pre_framework_v2_certification.items: All items certified before Framework v2 deployment (pre-S202)
pre_framework_v2_certification.pattern: No pre-flight gate existed. Items entered Certified state with DL-008 (539 occurrences), DL-026 (1,005 items), DL-021 (100 items), DL-030 (5 answer-key errors).
pre_framework_v2_certification.root_cause: Governance was manual discipline, not automated enforcement.

post_framework_v2_gap.pattern: Certification pipeline checked DL-008 (Rule 2) but not DL-026 (Rule 6 was not yet deployed). Items passed through a partial gate.
post_framework_v2_gap.root_cause: Governance guard coverage gap. Rule 6 deployed S814 — gap closed. 39 items identified for remediation (S813 C3).
post_framework_v2_gap.note: This is a governance coverage gap, not a manual workaround. But it demonstrates the risk: any gate that doesn't check all known defect patterns creates a bypass path.

detection_signals.signal: An item with question_state='Certified' has no corresponding readiness gate PASS record
detection_signals.automated_check: Audit: (certified_count_from_packs) vs (certified_count_with_gate_records). Any gap > 0 is a manual workaround or governance gap.

detection_signals.signal: A new governance guard rule is added, but items Certified before the rule was deployed still carry the defect
detection_signals.automated_check: After every new rule deployment, re-scan Certified pool for the defect class the rule blocks. Flag any pre-existing occurrences.

detection_signals.signal: A write to a pack file bypasses governance guard (e.g., direct manual edit outside tool tracking)
detection_signals.automated_check: Compare file modification timestamps against session records. Flag writes that occurred outside tracked sessions.

response_protocol.immediate: Block the item from learner pool delivery until pre-flight gates re-run and pass. Quarantine any affected QIDs.
response_protocol.remediation: Re-run pre-flight gates on affected items. If gates fail, remediate. Document the bypass and close the governance gap.
response_protocol.prevention: Governance automation (P5): all certification paths must pass through the same automated gate pipeline. No manual bypass paths. Every defect class with a known pattern must have a BLOCK-level governance guard rule.

drift_categories.description: Report files, scripts, or data artifacts that are produced but never consumed by any downstream tool, registry, or decision process
drift_categories.principle_violated: P2 Scan Once Consume Many + P6 Traceability Everywhere

report_explosion.peak: 29 report files in a single session (S726)
report_explosion.impact: Report files that are never consumed represent wasted agent effort and create noise that obscures genuinely important findings.

examples: SESSION301 — 26 agent outputs, many used only within S301 and never referenced subsequently
SESSION200-207 — architecture design sessions produced ~50+ report files, of which ~15 feed ongoing operations
Root directory — 848 files in reports/ root, many with SESSION_ prefix indicating they were session-specific outputs
one_off_patterns.impact: One-off reports create a discovery problem — finding the authoritative report on any topic requires searching through hundreds of files.

detection_signals.signal: A report file exists in reports/ that is not referenced by any registry, consuming tool, or cross-reference document
detection_signals.automated_check: Build a report-consumption graph: for each file in reports/, check if it is referenced by any file in knowledge/ (CURRENT_BASELINES, DEFECT_LIBRARY, REVISION_HISTORY, CAQS), governance/, or scripts/. Unreferenced files are untracked artifacts.

detection_signals.signal: New report files are produced without a designated consumer in the session's output manifest
detection_signals.automated_check: Session closeout check: every report file produced must have a documented consumer (a tool, a registry, a decision board, or a subsequent session). Files without a consumer are untracked by default.

response_protocol.immediate: None — untracked artifacts are not emergency. They are waste, not risk.
response_protocol.remediation: Archive one-off reports that have no future consumption path. Catalog remaining reports and link to relevant registries.
response_protocol.prevention: Session planning must include output-consumer mapping. No report should be produced without knowing who consumes it and when.

drift_categories.description: Entities referenced in one registry are absent from another, or registry claims disagree with raw source files

P1-EC-004_state_inconsistency.entities: P1-EC-004 (Pack C Section E, Domain E)
P1-EC-004_state_inconsistency.discrepancy: Investigation API reported question_state 'Unprocessed'. REVISION_HISTORY.md recorded certification in S853.
P1-EC-004_state_inconsistency.root_cause: Registry staleness — Investigation API consumed a pre-S853 registry snapshot.
P1-EC-004_state_inconsistency.status: Flagged in S254 cross-engine consistency audit. Pending reconciliation.
P1-EC-004_state_inconsistency.learner_impact: None (question is correctly Certified in raw file, delivery mechanism reads raw file question_state).

DL-019_concurrent_write_data_loss.discrepancy: DL-008 remediation (Session A: 149 clears) was overwritten by DL-013 certification wave (Session B: wrote from pre-Session-A snapshot).
DL-019_concurrent_write_data_loss.root_cause: No file-lock or session-coordination mechanism. Two sessions operating on same files with different disk snapshots.
DL-019_concurrent_write_data_loss.impact: Had to re-remediate 432 items across 16 batches. No learner impact because items were non-Certified.

detection_signals.signal: A registry reports an entity state that differs from the raw source file's state
detection_signals.automated_check: Cross-engine consistency scan (S254 pattern): for each entity type, compare registry claims against raw file values. Flag any mismatch.
detection_signals.frequency: Per certification wave or per session with write operations

detection_signals.signal: A session modifies a pack file but REVISION_HISTORY.md is not updated
detection_signals.automated_check: Governance guard Rule 1 WARN — detected at session idle. question_state changes without REVISION_HISTORY.md update trigger warning.

detection_signals.signal: The same pack file is modified by two concurrent sessions
detection_signals.automated_check: Before every write to a pack file, verify no other session has written since the T0 hash capture. Hash mismatch at Tend without corresponding REVISION_HISTORY.md entry indicates concurrent write.

response_protocol.immediate: For registry-vs-raw discrepancy: quarantine the registry claim. Trust the raw file. Flag for reconciliation.
response_protocol.remediation: Re-run the registry generator from raw files. Update stale consumers. Document the root cause of the staleness.
response_protocol.prevention: Traceability Everywhere principle. Every entity must have a single authoritative source. Registries must be re-generated from raw files before any operation that consumes them.

tmid_checkpoint.description: Mid-session or after 2+ agents complete — verify no drift introduced

tend_checkpoint.description: Session closeout — final drift check and REVISION_HISTORY.md entry
checks: Certified count verified unchanged (read-only sessions) or documented change (write sessions)

automatic_escalation.description: Drift signals that trigger immediate governance intervention

signals.signal: Unexpected hash change in any baseline file
signals.action: Halt all agents; spawn governance agent; run G1-G5 reconciliation (Session 31 runbook)
Halt all pack-write agents; re-parse via Function constructor
Spawn ledger-reconciliation agent; verify via direct grep

signals.signal: Two agents report different defect counts for same (class, pack)
signals.action: Independent third-agent verification; require QID-list evidence

signals.signal: New governance guard rule deployed but Certified items carry the defect

signals.action: Halt consumers of conflicting registries; reconcile against raw files
